newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Chief Secretary to stay on in job after handover.
newsitem.headline: HK Chief Secretary to stay on in job after handover.

text.p: Hong Kong's Chief Secretary Anson Chan said on Saturday she has accepted a request by chief executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa to stay on in her job after the territory reverts to Chinese rule next year.
"I'm extremely grateful to Mr Tung for requesting me to stay on and for his trust in me. I'm of course delighted to accept," Chan told reporters after a breakfast meeting with Tung.
Chan, Hong Kong's top civil servant and second-in-command to colonial Governor Chris Patten, enjoys a high degree of respect and popularity in the territory.
Tung was chosen by a 400-member China-backed Selection Committee earlier this month to become Hong Kong's first post-colonial leader after the territory reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
"I'm sure we'd have a very cooperative working relationship. We've worked together as colleagues for a few years. And she's also a very good friend," Tung said.
